tl;dr - we have to kill workers on "bazel clean" to fix this. I don't think there's a way we can keep them running without extending the protocol with a "cwd" field for each WorkRequest and fixing all workers to explicitly chdir into that directory before opening any files. I'll send a fix for the clean command.

Workaround: Until this is fixed, use either "bazel clean" without any flags (though that might still cause failures, see below), or to be on the safe side, just use "bazel clean --expunge".

What's happening:

The working directory of persistent worker processes is the execution root (cf. "bazel info execution_root"), unless the flag --worker_sandboxing is used, in which case it is "$output_base/bazel-workers/worker-$id-$mnemonic".

The reason why you see these failures is that the working directory of the running persistent workers is deleted under their feet by the "clean" command, so the next time they try to open a file, it'll fail.

Let's look at each case individually:

bazel clean: Bazel will delete the execution_root directory. The Bazel server keeps running. The next time "bazel build" runs, a new execution_root directory is created in the same path as the old one. In theory this should invalidate the current working directory of the worker process (because while the path is the same, the inode is different), but JavaBuilder doesn't seem to mind and continues working fine. I guess other workers might fail in this case, too.

bazel clean --async: Bazel will move the execroot and thus the current working directory. You can actually observe this using the "pwdx" tool on the running JavaBuilder processes:

```
philwo@philwo:~/bazel-test$ bazel clean --async
INFO: Reading 'startup' options from /usr/local/google/home/philwo/.bazelrc: --watchfs
INFO: Starting clean.
INFO: Output tree moved to /usr/local/google/home/philwo/.cache/bazel/_bazel_philwo/11ae71351ba9bcc6fe0988005a8d1396/execroot/bazel-test_tmp_30646 for deletion
philwo@philwo:~/bazel-test$ pwdx 1876
1876: /usr/local/google/home/philwo/.cache/bazel/_bazel_philwo/11ae71351ba9bcc6fe0988005a8d1396/execroot/bazel-test_tmp_30646 (deleted)
```

The next time the worker tries to open a file, it will find itself in a no longer existing working directory and will crash.

bazel --expunge / --expunge_async: Work, because the Bazel server quits after the command, thus all workers quit, too. I don't know why --expunge_async doesn't work - maybe it's generally buggy? But that is a different bug than the worker process crash here (the shown stack trace comes from inside Bazel itself).

oh, I had completely missed that there was a "bazel clean" in the middle. It's logical that cleaning things (asynchronously!) from under the worker's feet will lead to weirdness.

David, why are you running clean in the first place?

"changing the bazlets source wouldn't re-fetch the bazlets" 

what does that mean? Are you writing self-modifiying code?

> "changing the bazlets source wouldn't re-fetch the bazlets"

Two repositories:

* gitiles
* bazlets

Consider these CLs: [1], [2]. The former exposed `pkg_war` bazlet and the latter was using it. While working on it, I routed the bazlets to my local directory, as the commit wasn't yet pushed to bazlet to be consumed from:

```
  load_bazlets(
    commit = "a8a04c9ef2f131816c1e458613bee93b461ba652",
    local_path = "/home/davido/projects/bazlets",
)
```

After I have built it once, and `pkg_war` was fetched from the local bazlet repository located in `/home/davido/projects/bazlets`, i changed the `tools/pkg_war.bzl`, and re-built gitiles war in gitiles directory:

```
  $ cd gitiles
  $ bazel build gitiles
```

To make sure, that pkg_war bazlets is get re-fetched again, I issued `bazel clean && bazel build gitiles`.

* [1] https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/101150
* [2] https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/101071
but was that necessary? Did it not work without make clean? The bazlets have a commit SHA1, so it should pick up changes correctly.

I haven't committed anything in `bazlets` repository (only edited `pkg_war.bzl` in `emacs`) and haven't adapted/changed anything in `gitiles` repository. Note, that when `local_path` is passed to `load_bazlets` macro:

```
  load_bazlets(
        commit = "a8a04c9ef2f131816c1e458613bee93b461ba652",
        local_path = "/home/davido/projects/bazlets",
  )
```

then `git_repository` version without SHA1, but with path only is used: [1].

```
  native.local_repository(
       name = NAME,
       path = local_path,
  )
```

* [1] https://gerrit.googlesource.com/gitiles/+/f9bb416b3d35ee00bda17360e4d74ec8f6350d58/tools/bazlets.bzl#14
